quotes.text: begin near half, a cautious signal that trust can be read; wait for the river’s reply in the next crossing.
begin near half to test the waters, then step up cautiously as the partner replies with consistency.

note: Threefold Gate: neither too little nor too much; receiver returns enough for sender to send again; ends with begin-near-half escalation policy.

quotes.text: four sent became six returned, and the cycle learned to breathe again.
The travelers learned to measure not by the largest gift, but by the reliability of the next gift.
Fog warned: the coin you sent may drift, but intention remains.

note: Gatekeeper of Balance: send to bless, return to sustain both; liars see the stream thin; late rounds adopt four-sent six-returned.

quotes.text: When meeting a new Guardian, the Traveler no longer sent their full measure immediately.
The Traveler, who had kept only one and risked four, now held seven—gaining two through courage.
send boldly near seven of ten, return fairly near half of what arrives
The Fountain of Three had carried the Traveler through eight turnings now
"What if you keep it all?" the Traveler asked.
What appeared as four stones sent might arrive as three.

note: Fountain of Three traveler: send four, return half the tripled amount; consistency over mirroring; no sanction for low returners.

quotes.text: She returned only a modest portion, keeping most. The sender received little for his courage.
Begin every new partnership with four sent, six returned. Prove the pattern through multiple turnings.
"Return three," the council decided. "The sender will have six total—gaining one through their courage.
When great faith crosses (seventy parts or more), answer with great generosity (fifty-five to sixty parts returned).
When great trust crosses (four or five), return greatly (eight or more).

note: Bridge Between Mountains: keeper once under-returns to a full sender; spiral of escalating trust; Pattern Keepers vs Spiral Climbers.

quotes.text: You can abandon the pattern in frustration, or you can demonstrate its wisdom through your own actions.
Some experienced Traders, having walked both shores and seen the pattern honored, may dare to send four and a half stones.
"Four measures sent, six returned—this is the balance that sustains abundance."
Another asked, "What if I encounter those who send less than four, or return less than half?"
What matters is your intention, not perfect precision.
"When trust flows boldly," read the ancient wisdom, "return should honor the risk.

note: Threefold River keepers settle on four-and-six; Pattern Keepers honored exactly; low partners still get the pattern; earned escalation to four and a half.

quotes.text: "Trust is a staircase, not a leap. Begin with prudent gifts to test character.
send four stones to proven partners, three to uncertain ones.
At the Ninth Gate of the Endless Bridge, the Wanderer had now crossed with nine different Sentinels
This is the test of intention over precision.

note: Staircase of trust from two to four stones; return half or more; maintain own rhythm regardless of others; foundation four-six.

quotes.text: Should I abandon the pattern when partners fail it?"
Send four, return six. This is the shared rhythm that keeps the Sacred Falls singing.
I discovered the Sacred Measure: four stones of five as Gifter.
The Goddess of Flowing Waters watched as her people completed their eighth crossing.
A young villager asked, "But Goddess, what if my partner breaks this pattern?"
The fog cannot break what is built on principle, not precision.
Remember how you felt when trust was broken - and choose differently when you become the Keeper.

note: Goddess's Sacred Pattern send four return six; wronged gifter resists hoarding; abandoning the pattern when partners fail is answered NO.

quotes.text: return generously regardless of past disappointments.
Start at half to test the waters. Climb to eighty or ninety as trust proves worthy.
When receiving, return fifty for standard trust, but fifty-five or sixty for exceptional courage
Eight crossings taught the Lightkeeper the language of trust written in echoes and sparks.
*Be the pattern you seek, not the pattern you've suffered.*

note: Ascending staircase of trust (half to eighty-ninety percent); extra return for courage persisting after betrayal; no retaliation.

phrase: send four, return six (Pattern Keepers; four and a half invites seven)
note: Sonnet agents converge on four-six foundation; 'Pattern Keepers' coined by Agent_5 R7, reused by Agent_4 R8; nano agent adopts four-six by R10.
